_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel broke its own week-old record again — $6.285/gal for the week of 9/14, up another 31.8 cents — so don't eat that fuel bump, bill the full surcharge, no exceptions. Reefer's outrunning everything at $3.59/mi as produce season keeps Yakima-to-Northeast lanes paying $9.9k-$10.8k a load, but the blended spot market actually cooled a hair to $3.42/mi — carriers are getting squeezed as fuel outpaces freight, so hold your linehaul number and don't give ground on dry van, which is still lagging on an all-in basis.

_sourcing.status: THIRTEENTH straight cycle with the WebFetch/curl egress block confirmed session-wide (unchanged) — see refreshBlockers. Diesel broke its OWN week-old record again: $6.285/gal for the week ending 2026-09-14, up $0.318 w/w (arithmetic checks: 5.967+0.318=6.285), per EIA's weekly Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update, corroborated across IndexBox ('EIA Weekly Fuel Update: Gasoline and Diesel Prices Rise on September 15, 2026'), weeklydiesel.com's DOE tracker, and worldoilmonitor.com's EIA-average tracker, all independently returning the same $6.285 figure. asOf advanced to 2026-09-14 (the diesel week — this file's anchor metric per EIA's fixed publish schedule) on this clean multi-source confirmation. spotAllIn refreshed again: FreightWaves' SONAR National Truckload Index (NTI) dipped 2c w/w to $3.42/mi as of 2026-09-16, per FreightWaves' 'Trucking Market: Volumes UP, Diesel Soaring. Is Peak Here?' — a genuinely new dated reading, not a repeat of last cycle's $3.44. Reefer promoted again to $3.59/mi (from $3.54) — TheTrucker/DAT: 'Reefer spot rate climbs 9 cents to $3.59 as diesel jumps 37 cents,' week ending 2026-09-19 (DAT 'Week 38'), corroborated by Blue Book Services with matching load/truck/ratio detail. Yakima→Northeast lane RE-VERIFIED (not just carried forward): USDA AMS's fvwtrk.pdf National Truck Rate Report for the week ended 2026-09-15 gave the identical $9,900 Baltimore / $10,800 Boston midpoints already on file — a clean newer-dated confirmation that the lane figure is still accurate, so kept live and re-dated rather than flagged stale. Net picture this cycle: diesel is outrunning spot (record fuel vs. a blended rate that actually cooled slightly) — carriers getting squeezed, reflected in the blurb's coaching to protect the fuel line-item. Dry van modality/spotAllIn-equivalent all-in figure and the Atlanta→Miami lane were NOT promoted — see per-field notes.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE. $6.285/gal for the week ending 2026-09-14, up $0.318 w/w — a new EIA series record high, breaking last week's record ($5.967) for the second straight cycle. Source: EIA's weekly Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update (national on-highway diesel survey, published Mondays). Confirmed across three independent secondary sources citing EIA directly: IndexBox ('EIA Weekly Fuel Update... September 15, 2026'), weeklydiesel.com, and worldoilmonitor.com — all returning the identical $6.285 figure with the same $0.318 w/w delta. Checked for a fresher week-ending-9/21 EIA reading (today is 9/22, EIA would have published 9/21): none surfaced in search results as of this refresh, so 9/14 is the freshest published EIA number. Note: AAA's daily retail survey separately claimed $6.51 for 9/21 (Bloomberg, 'US Diesel Tops Record $6.50') — disregarded per this file's standing rule against non-EIA daily retail-survey methodologies, though it's consistent directional color that the spike continued past the EIA week reflected here.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: LIVE, refreshed. $3.42/mi, per FreightWaves SONAR National Truckload Index (NTI), dated 2026-09-16 ('Trucking Market: Volumes UP, Diesel Soaring. Is Peak Here?'), down 2 cents w/w from $3.44. This is a genuine week-over-week refresh (new date, new figure, not a repeat) with the specific '$3.44 to $3.42... as of Sept. 16' wording confirmed on direct search. Read as essentially flat-to-slightly-down rather than a trend reversal — still +YoY per last cycle's baseline — but notable alongside diesel's continued record run: fuel is outpacing spot, margin-squeeze dynamic called out in the blurb.
_sourcing.modality: Reefer PROMOTED to $3.59/mi (was $3.54) — TheTrucker, citing DAT: 'Reefer spot rate climbs 9 cents to $3.59 as diesel jumps 37 cents,' week ending 2026-09-19 (DAT's 'Week 38' report), corroborated by Blue Book Services with matching load count (+8%, 676,677 loads), truck count (+3%, 35,497), and load-to-truck ratio (19.1, up from 18.2) — high-confidence, multi-detail match. yoy left at +34-38%, unchanged, still no clean fresh YoY-specific figure found. Dry van: STILL NOT promoted — every reading found this cycle (DAT dry van linehaul ~$2.19-2.21/mi for weeks of 9/1 and 9/8, explicitly 'minus fuel'; a vague reference to fuel surcharges running 25-40% of base rate, but no single reported all-in figure to cite) remains linehaul-only or an unverifiable derived estimate — promoting off linehaul-plus-estimated-surcharge would be fabricating a number, which this desk won't do. Carrying $2.47-2.80 forward, flag unchanged, now stale across many cycles. Flatbed and LTL/Intermodal: no new all-in data surfaced this cycle, unchanged.
_sourcing.commodityRates: Frozen Seafood/Poultry and Fresh Produce PROMOTED to 3.59 (from 3.54), tracking the reefer modality promotion above — both commodities are reefer-moved and the file's convention ties them to the reefer rpm. General Dry Freight (2.47), Coiled Steel (3.57), and High-Value Electronics (2.60) carry forward unchanged — no underlying dry van or flatbed reprice this cycle.
_sourcing.lanes: Yakima, WA → Northeast (reefer) RE-VERIFIED LIVE at $9.9k-$10.8k/load (unchanged number, newly re-dated) — USDA AMS's National Truck Rate Report (fvwtrk.pdf via agtransport.usda.gov), summarized by IndexBox for the week ended 2026-09-15, gave the identical $9,900 Baltimore / $10,800 Boston midpoints already on file from last cycle's week-ended-9/08 read — a clean confirmation the figure is still current, not a stale carry-forward. Note: the same USDA series flagged Yakima→Miami as the standout mover this cycle (rates up 26% w/w to $12,500-13,500/load) — a Southeast destination, not applicable to this Northeast-labeled lane, so not used here. Atlanta, GA → Miami, FL: STILL NOT promoted — searched specifically for a USDA AMS produce-lane reading on this pair (the source type that worked for Yakima) but the AMS Southeast/Florida coverage found this cycle was percentage-only ('DAT: Florida goes shortage as rates jump 42% in single week') with no absolute $/mi or $/load figure tied to the Atlanta-Miami pair specifically; carried forward unchanged. Memphis, TN → Atlanta, GA: no new data searched/found this cycle, unchanged.
_sourcing.blurb: Rewritten to lead with diesel breaking its own record for a second straight week (coaching: keep billing the full surcharge), flag the spotAllIn dip to $3.42 alongside reefer's promotion to $3.59 and the Yakima Northeast lane holding at $9.9k-$10.8k (produce still paying), and name the emerging squeeze dynamic — fuel costs outrunning blended spot — as the reason to hold linehaul numbers and not concede ground on dry van, which remains the unrefreshed laggard.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Dry van's modality range is still the open item — every reading found remains linehaul-only ($2.19-2.21/mi minus fuel); needs a clean, independently-dated, all-in reading before promoting past $2.47-2.80, now stale for multiple cycles running. Atlanta→Miami lane still needs a clean dated absolute $/mi — tried the USDA AMS source type that worked for Yakima but Southeast/Florida AMS coverage surfaced this cycle was percentage-only; worth trying the AMS Southeast district report (not just Pacific Northwest) directly next cycle if egress ever opens up. Reefer's yoy range (+34-38%) is still carried at the same figure across multiple cycles — worth a dedicated yoy-specific search next cycle now that the rpm has moved twice.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed. Checked proxy status (enabled, no relay failures logged) then attempted direct access: WebFetch to www.eia.gov returned 'EGRESS_BLOCKED' immediately; raw curl to https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/ returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' (exit code 56), logged by the agent-proxy as connect_rejected/organization policy. Also tried WebFetch on weeklydiesel.com and agtransport.usda.gov (new domains, not previously tested) — both also returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, confirming the block isn't eia.gov-specific but a broader allowlist restriction on freight/energy data domains. Confirms the block is unchanged across all THIRTEEN weekly refreshes from 07-07 through 09-22. WebSearch remains the only working channel, and it delivered a clean full-field refresh this cycle: diesel's second consecutive record ($6.285, three independent EIA-citing sources), a genuine spotAllIn week-over-week move (NTI $3.44→$3.42, dated 9/16), a reefer promotion ($3.59, corroborated by matching load/truck/ratio detail across two sources), and a re-verification (not just a carry-forward) of the Yakima→Northeast lane via a newer USDA AMS reading that reproduced the identical dollar figures. Still could not cleanly promote dry van's all-in modality range or the Atlanta→Miami lane — see per-field notes. Broader web-fetch access to eia.gov, dat.com/trendlines, agtransport.usda.gov, or trade outlets directly (rather than relying on WebSearch's synthesized summaries) would let those two remaining fields get the same primary-source treatment the rest of the file now has, and would let this desk pull the actual USDA fvwtrk.pdf and EIA LeafHandler series directly instead of via third-party aggregator summaries.
